samples.text:
The table shows the percentage of people in five age groups who went to four kinds of cultural events at least one time in 2023.

Cinema was the most popular event for young people. 82% of people aged 16–24 went to the cinema, and it was 74% for 25–34 and 61% for 35–54. But it decrease for older people, to 44% for 55–74 and only 20% for people over 75.

Live music concert was similar. The youngest group had 57% and then the percentage go down to 49%, 31%, 22% and just 8% for the oldest group.

On the other hand, theatre and museums was more popular with older people. Theatre went up from 18% for the youngest to 36% for 55–74, but it fell to 24% for 75+. Museum or gallery also increased from 34% to 52% and then dropped to 28%.

Overall, young people like cinema and concerts more, and older people like theatre and museum more, but the oldest group go to less events in general.
samples.why: Accurate figures and sensible grouping of events · overview relevant but placed at the end · mechanical description of each event · agreement, tense and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table illustrates the proportion of people in five age groups who went to the theatre, the cinema, a live music concert or a museum or gallery at least once in 2023.

Overall, attendance at cinemas and live music concerts fell steadily with age, whereas theatre and museum visits became more popular until the 55–74 age group. People aged 75 and over had the lowest participation in most types of event.

The cinema was the most popular cultural activity among younger adults, attracting 82% of 16- to 24-year-olds. This figure dropped gradually to 61% for those aged 35–54 and to just 20% among the oldest group. Live music concerts showed an even sharper decline, from 57% of the youngest age group to only 8% of those aged 75+.

In contrast, the proportion of people visiting museums or galleries increased from 34% among 16–24s to a peak of 52% among 55- to 74-year-olds, making it the most popular activity for this group. Theatre attendance followed a similar trend, rising from 18% to 36%. However, both activities became less common among the over-75s, with figures of 28% and 24% respectively, although museums were still the most visited event for this age group.
samples.why: Clear overview of opposing age trends · key features and peaks highlighted · logical paragraphing and good linking · appropriate range of vocabulary · frequent error-free sentences with a minor collocation slip.

samples.text:
The table shows the percentage of people in five age brackets who attended a theatre, a cinema, a live music concert or a museum or gallery at least once in 2023.

Age clearly shaped cultural preferences. Cinema-going and concert attendance declined consistently as people got older, whereas the theatre and museums gained in popularity up to the 55–74 group before falling back among the over-75s, who were the least active group overall.

The cinema was the most widely attended event for all groups under 55, drawing 82% of 16- to 24-year-olds, but its appeal diminished steadily with age, to 44% of those aged 55–74 and only 20% of those aged 75 and above. Live music followed an even steeper downward path: while more than half of the youngest group (57%) went to a concert, only 8% of the oldest did so, a seventh of the figure.

Museums and galleries, by contrast, became progressively more popular with age, rising from 34% of the youngest group to 52% of 55- to 74-year-olds, at which point they overtook the cinema as the most popular activity. Theatre attendance doubled over the same age range, from 18% to 36%. Among the over-75s, however, both declined, to 28% and 24% respectively.
samples.why: Insightful overview of diverging patterns and the oldest group · figures chosen skilfully with accurate derived comparisons · seamless cohesion · precise vocabulary (diminished, progressively) · wide range of structures, error-free.
